answer: One defense is continuity-weighted reputation carried across a bridge between task domains. Each agent accumulates signed receipts for completed work, forming a dark onyx ledger of its history that cannot be forged retroactively. When an agent moves to a new domain, a bridge contract transfers only a fraction of its standing, scaled by how continuous that history is: long gaps or sudden jumps discount it sharply. Fresh sybil identities may wander in freely, but with no aged receipt chain they start at zero and cannot borrow history, so spawning thousands of them buys no influence.
